2 Data Import - MAG Catalogue 2.1 Overview WARNING: This is the MAG catalogue from short-read assemblies and not hybrid assemblies with PacBio. This chapter prepares the Metagenome-Assembled Genome (MAG) catalogue for downstream analyses. All data processing steps are shown for transparency, but code chunks are set to eval=FALSE so they do not execute during bookdown compilation. The processed data is saved to .Rdata files which are then loaded in subsequent plotting chapters. 2.2 Genome (MAGs) Catalogue Relevant metadata of genomes are fetched and merged into one genome metadata object for downstream analyses. This includes taxonomic classification, quality metrics, phylogenetic trees, and functional annotations. Location on ERDA: ID: ELPE6LATFN Path: 3D-omics/processed_data/f_mg-mg_assembly Access: read genome_taxonomy: https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/ELPE6LATFN/results/prokaryotes/annotate/gtdbtk.summary.tsv genome_quality: https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/ELPE6LATFN/results/prokaryotes/annotate/checkm2.quality_report.tsv genome_tree: https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/ELPE6LATFN/results/prokaryotes/annotate/gtdbtk.backbone.bac120.classify.tree genome_annotations: https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/ELPE6LATFN/results/prokaryotes/annotate/dram.annotations.tsv.gz The number of genomes in these files should match the number of genomes in the count tables, after accounting for the appropriate dereplication at species level. I find the drep.0.95.fa.gz file on ERDA. To find which genomes exist at 0.95 dereplication level I do the following in the terminal: cd OneDrive - University of Copenhagen cd Documents/Github projects/Adenovirus/data/MAG_catalogue gunzip drep.0.95.fa.gz grep “^>” drep.0.95.fa | sed ‘s/>//’ > genome_names.tsv cut -d’@’ -f1 genome_names.tsv | sort -u > unique_genome_names.tsv 2.2.1 Dereplicated Genomes Bins were initially dereplicated at 99%, and annotations generated for all resulting MAGs. A second dereplication was performed at 95% to yield species-representative genomes. This analysis is performed on that subset. Note: The drep.0.95.fa file must be processed first using terminal commands (shown in comments above) to extract unique genome names. # Read list of genomes at 95% dereplication level # This file is generated from the drep.0.95.fa file using terminal commands # Note: warning=FALSE suppresses vroom parsing warnings (e.g., inconsistent column types) selected_genomes <- read_tsv("data/MAG_catalogue/unique_genome_names.tsv", col_names = "genome") # Report number of species-representative genomes nrow(selected_genomes) The dereplication yielded 251 species-representative genomes that will be used for all downstream analyses. 2.2.2 Genome (MAGs) Taxonomy This section processes the raw taxonomy table generated by GTDBtk and simplifies it for downstream analyses. Taxonomic classifications are parsed, cleaned, and formatted consistently. # Load and process GTDBtk taxonomy summary file # This contains taxonomic classifications for all MAGs at species level dereplication # Note: Some rows have "N/A" in numeric columns (msa_percent, translation_table), # which causes parsing warnings. We suppress these and handle them properly. genome_taxonomy <- read_tsv( "data/MAG_catalogue/gtdbtk.summary.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE, na = c("", "N/A", "NA") # Treat "N/A" as missing values ) %>% # Rename first column to standardize naming rename(genome = user_genome) %>% # Remove .fa extension from genome names for consistency mutate(genome = str_replace_all(genome, "\\.fa", "")) %>% # Filter to only include species-representative genomes (95% dereplication) filter(genome %in% selected_genomes$genome) %>% # Parse the classification string into separate taxonomic level columns # GTDBtk format: d__Domain;p__Phylum;c__Class;o__Order;f__Family;g__Genus;s__Species separate(classification, c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"), sep = ";") %>% # Remove GTDBtk prefix letters (d__, p__, etc.) from each taxonomic level mutate(across(domain:species, ~ str_sub(., 4))) %>% # Select relevant taxonomic columns for downstream use select(genome, domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species) %>% # Handle missing or unclassified species names mutate( species = if_else( is.na(species) | species == "", paste0("unclassified_", genus), # Use genus name if species missing species ) ) %>% # Handle cases where both species and genus are unclassified mutate( species = if_else( is.na(species) | species == "unclassified_", paste0("unclassified_", family), # Use family name if both missing species ) ) %>% # Handle missing genus names mutate( genus = if_else( is.na(genus) | genus == "", paste0("unclassified_", family), genus ) ) %>% # Handle duplicate species names by adding suffixes (_sp1, _sp2, etc.) group_by(species) %>% mutate( species = if (n() > 1) paste0(species, "_sp", row_number()) else species ) %>% ungroup() # Rename Bacillota_I to Bacillota for consistency with other MAG catalogues genome_taxonomy <- genome_taxonomy %>% mutate(phylum = case_when( phylum == "Bacillota_I" ~ "Bacillota", TRUE ~ phylum # Keep all other phylum values as-is )) 2.2.3 Genome (MAGs) Quality Quality properties of the genomes are assessed using CheckM2, which provides completeness, contamination, and other quality metrics for each MAG. # Load CheckM2 quality report # This contains completeness, contamination, genome size, and other quality metrics # Note: warning=FALSE suppresses vroom parsing warnings (e.g., inconsistent column types) genome_quality <- read_tsv("data/MAG_catalogue/checkm2.quality_report.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% # Rename first column (genome name column) rename(genome = 1) %>% # Remove .fa extension from genome names for consistency mutate(genome = str_replace_all(genome, "\\.fa", "")) %>% # Filter to only include species-representative genomes (95% dereplication) filter(genome %in% selected_genomes$genome) %>% # Select and rename relevant quality metric columns select(genome, Completeness, Contamination, Coding_Density, Genome_Size, Contig_N50) %>% rename(completeness = Completeness, contamination = Contamination, coding_density = Coding_Density, length = Genome_Size, N50_length = Contig_N50) %>% # Calculate circularity indicator: N50/length ratio # If N50 >= length, the genome is likely circularized mutate(circularity = N50_length/length) %>% mutate(circularity = ifelse(circularity >= 1, "1", "0")) %>% # For circularized genomes, assume 100% completeness and 0% contamination mutate(completeness = ifelse(circularity == "1", 100, completeness), contamination = ifelse(circularity == "1", 0, contamination)) %>% # Calculate length ratio relative to median bacterial genome length # This helps identify unusually large or small genomes mutate(length_ratio = length/median(length, na.rm = TRUE)) # Report number of circularized genomes cat("Number of circularized genomes:", sum(genome_quality$circularity == "1"), "\n") 2.2.4 Genome (MAGs) Phylogenetic Tree This section loads and processes the phylogenetic tree generated by GTDBtk. The tree is pruned to include only the species-representative genomes used in this analysis. Note that the archaeal tree is only generated if archaea are detected among the genomes. # Load GTDBtk phylogenetic tree (bacterial backbone tree) genome_tree <- read.tree("data/MAG_catalogue/gtdbtk.backbone.bac120.classify.tree") # Remove single quotes from tip labels (genome names) for consistency genome_tree$tip.label <- str_replace_all(genome_tree$tip.label, "'", "") # Prune tree to keep only tips corresponding to selected genomes (95% dereplication) genome_tree <- keep.tip(genome_tree, tip = selected_genomes$genome) Note: If there are unmatched tip labels between the tree and selected genomes, this indicates some genome names don’t match between the tree file and the dereplication list. This may need manual checking. It was giving error: Error in keep.tip.phylo(genome_tree, tip = selected_genomes$genome) : unmatched tip labels: TH4_04:bin_000018 I will remove this taxon. 2.2.5 Merged Genome (MAGs) taxonomy & quality Merge taxonomy, length and quality information genome_metadata <- genome_taxonomy %>% left_join(genome_quality, by = join_by(genome == genome)) genome_metadata$order <- gsub("-", "_", genome_metadata$order) genome_metadata <- genome_metadata[match(genome_tree$tip.label, genome_metadata$genome), ] 2.2.5.1 Factoring of taxonomic levels phylum_metadata <- genome_metadata %>% group_by(phylum) %>% summarize( # Count the microsamples `number_of_genera` = n_distinct(genus), # Collect unique values separated by commas genus = paste(unique(genus), collapse = ", "), phylum = paste(unique(phylum), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>% select(phylum, number_of_genera, genus) %>% # Preserve original order arrange(match(phylum, unique(genome_metadata$phylum))) order_metadata <- genome_metadata %>% group_by(order) %>% summarize( # Count the microsamples `number_of_genera` = n_distinct(genus), # Collect unique values separated by commas genus = paste(unique(genus), collapse = ", "), phylum = paste(unique(phylum), collapse = ", "), class = paste(unique(class), collapse = ", "), # Ensure the dataframe is ungrouped .groups = "drop") %>% select(phylum, class, order, number_of_genera, genus) %>% # Preserve original order arrange(match(order, unique(genome_metadata$order))) phylum_level_vector <- as.character(unique(phylum_metadata$phylum)) order_level_vector <- as.character(unique(order_metadata$order)) 2.2.6 Genome (MAGs) functional annotations This is the raw annotation table generated by DRAM, which is used to generate GIFT data using distillR. # Load DRAM functional annotations # Note: warning=FALSE suppresses vroom parsing warnings (e.g., inconsistent column types) genome_annotations <- read_tsv("data/MAG_catalogue/dram.annotations.tsv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% rename(gene = 1, genome = 2) genome_annotations <- genome_annotations %>% filter(genome %in% selected_genomes$genome) 2.2.7 Distil functional annotations Raw functional annotations are distilled into genome-inferred functional traits to generate biologically more meaningful functional traits for downstream analyses. genome_gifts <- distill(genome_annotations, GIFT_db, genomecol = 2, annotcol = c(9, 10, 19)) 2.3 Bacterial phyla & order color scheme data phylum_colors <- c(Actinomycetota = "#346254", Bacillota = "#4a6ab7", Bacillota_A = "#8c1c47", Bacillota_B = "#644ca3", Bacillota_C = "#144f5c", Bacillota_G = "#990000", Bacteroidota = "#9c8464", Cyanobacteriota = "#b45f06", Desulfobacterota = "#462410", Pseudomonadota = "#c49d4b" ) order_colors <- c(Actinomycetales = "#79b1a3", Coriobacteriales = "#498a77", Acholeplasmatales = "#cfe2f3", CAJFEE01 = "#a0c5e8", Erysipelotrichales = "#7acef4", Lactobacillales = "#6390fb", ML615J_28 = "#70c9de", RF39 = "#5c7fba", RFN20 = "#6390bb", MOL361 = "#70a8dc", Christensenellales = "#f58262", Clostridiales = "#cf4a82", Lachnospirales = "#e15f7d", Monoglobales = "#e18299", Oscillospirales = "#ba2760", Peptostreptococcales = "#e35d51", TANB77 = "#ef3d26", UBA1381 = "#be5643", UBA1212 = "#cc0100", HGM11327 = "#d04c68", Eubacteriales = "#c93232", Peptococcales = "#d9d2e9", UBA4068 = "#b4a7d6", UBA7702 = "#8e7cc3", Veillonellales = "#2c7c91", DTUO25 = "#cc1a1a", Gastranaerophilales = "#e69138", Desulfovibrionales = "#8b4e2e", Bacteroidales = "#e3c7a0", Enterobacterales = "#ffcc62", RF32 = "#f2d78c", Rs_D84 = "#f2c98e", Verrucomicrobiales = "#823f1d") 2.4 Save Working Objects In the last step, the objects needed for downstream analyses are saved to .Rdata files. Objects are split into logical groups to keep file sizes manageable for GitHub. 2.4.1 Save Core MAG Catalogue Data (for plotting chapters) # Save core MAG catalogue objects used in plotting chapters save( genome_tree, genome_metadata, phylum_level_vector, order_level_vector, genome_gifts, file = "data/MAG_catalogue/data.Rdata" ) 2.4.2 Save Color Schemes (for plotting chapters) # Save color schemes and plotting theme for downstream plots # Note: treatment_colours_bright and custom_ggplot_theme will be added in 01B save( phylum_colors, order_colors, file = "data/data_colors.Rdata" ) 2.4.3 Save Complete Preparation Data (for colleagues’ analyses) For colleagues who need access to all preparation data for additional analyses or plotting, the data is saved in multiple smaller files organized by data type: # 12 Diversity Partitioning Analysis 12.1 Overview This chapter performs hierarchical additive partitioning of alpha diversity to quantify how diversity is distributed across different hierarchical levels (within and among animals, treatments, and breeds). Note: This analysis requires specific functions for hierarchical partitioning that are defined within this chapter. 12.2 Load Data and Plotting Utilities # Load processed plotting data and color schemes load("data/macro/plot_data.Rdata") load("data/data_colors.Rdata") 12.3 Hierarchical Diversity Partitioning Functions These functions are used to calculate and visualize hierarchical additive partitioning of diversity. # Function to calculate hierarchical additive partitioning # Function to calculate hierarchical additive partitioning hier_adipart <- function(comm, hier, nsim = 999) { comm_bin <- (as.matrix(comm) > 0) * 1 alpha_obs <- mean(rowSums(comm_bin)) get_level_richness <- function(fac) { tapply(seq_len(nrow(comm_bin)), fac, function(idx) { sum(colSums(comm_bin[idx, , drop = FALSE]) > 0) }) |> mean() } level_names <- names(hier) level_rich <- sapply(hier, get_level_richness) gamma_obs <- sum(colSums(comm_bin) > 0) # exactly L betas betas <- c(level_rich[1] - alpha_obs, diff(level_rich)) names(betas) <- paste0("beta (", level_names, ")") observed <- c(alpha = alpha_obs, betas, gamma = gamma_obs) stat_fun <- function(x) { x <- (x > 0) * 1 alpha <- mean(rowSums(x)) lvl <- sapply(hier, function(fac) { tapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), fac, function(idx) sum(colSums(x[idx, , drop = FALSE]) > 0)) |> mean() }) gamma <- sum(colSums(x) > 0) betas <- c(lvl[1] - alpha, diff(lvl)) # select relevant batches filter(EX_batch %in% c("EXB020","EXB021")) %>% unnest(c(nucleic_acid, animal, SU_coordinate)) %>% # select relevant columns select(EX_batch, extract, animal, tube_barcode, RNA_concentration, elution_uL, nucleic_acid, SU_coordinate) %>% filter(nucleic_acid == "RNA") %>% # Step 1: Filter samples based on quality criteria # Requirements: RNA concentration > 30 ng/uL, non-missing values, specific time points rna_filtered <- RNA_extract_sample_div_metadata_macro %>% filter( !is.na(RNA_concentration), !is.na(richness), RNA_concentration > 30, (animal_breed == "broiler" & age %in% c(5, 14) | animal_breed == "layer" & age %in% c(7, 14) | age == 0) # optional: include day 0 controls ) # Step 2: Rank samples by combined score # Normalize metrics to 0-1 scale and create weighted combined score # Weight: 60% RNA concentration, 40% richness (prioritizes RNA quality) rna_ranked <- rna_filtered %>% mutate( #
